question.explanation: False celebrity death reports long predate social media. The article describes cases ranging from Mark Twain and Frank Sinatra to internet-era rumors about actors, musicians, and online personalities.
question.criteria: A named person explicitly identified in the opening or “Celebrities” section of the supplied death-hoax article as the subject of a false death report. People mentioned only as having actually died do not count.

provenance.brief: Name a celebrity who was the subject of a false death hoax.

quotes.Abe Vigoda: Abe Vigoda, seen here on Barney Miller in 1977, was mistakenly reported as dead many times before his actual death in 2016.
quotes.Mark Twain:
The report of my illness grew out of his illness; the report of my death was an exaggeration."
— Mark Twain, 1897.
quotes.Charlie Chaplin: in 1945 following the death of Franklin Roosevelt, there were hoax reports of the deaths of Charlie Chaplin and Frank Sinatra, among other celebrities of the time.
quotes.Frank Sinatra: in 1945 following the death of Franklin Roosevelt, there were hoax reports of the deaths of Charlie Chaplin and Frank Sinatra, among other celebrities of the time.
quotes.Paul McCartney: Possibly the most famous hoax of this type was the "Paul is dead" rumor, which claimed that Paul McCartney died in a car crash in 1966 and was replaced by a look-alike.
quotes.Eddie Murphy: Paul Walker's death on 30 November 2013 sparked rumors of Eddie Murphy dying in a snowboarding accident.
